evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（香港中文大學）
evidence.field: 乍；形義通解、甲骨文與早期用例
evidence.text: The database describes 乍 as an early graph for clearing vegetation, citing oracle-bone examples 乙8502 for clearing land and 合集13509 for building a settlement. It traces extensions to labor, construction and casting, and says 人 was added to distinguish 作 (labor/work) after 乍 was used for sudden or temporary meanings. It also cites bronze inscriptions for casting, building, making law and ‘serving as’ a standard, plus Warring States bamboo slips for both ‘serve as’ and ‘suddenly/temporarily.’ These are source analyses and cited examples, not a chronology inferred from a gloss list.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭 乍

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（香港中文大學）
evidence.field: 乍；《說文》 and phonological metadata
evidence.text: The page records the Shuowen gloss for 乍 as 止也, ‘stop,’ with an alternate gloss 亡也, and gives Guangyun 鋤駕 and a Middle Chinese category entry. The same page separately argues from oracle-bone forms for a vegetation-clearing sense and identifies 乍 as an early graph associated with 柞. This shows that the Shuowen account and modern paleographic analysis differ; the dictionary labels the ancient forms but their images were not inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭 乍

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（香港中文大學）
evidence.field: 作; relationship of 人 and 乍
evidence.text: The 乍 entry states that 人 was added as a semantic marker in 作 when 乍 acquired sudden/temporary uses. This supports a differentiation account in which 作 continues the work/action reading. It is not evidence that 作’s 人 component identifies a particular person or maker, and the database’s account does not by itself establish whether 乍 functioned as a phonetic component at the time 作 was formed.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭 乍

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 online text with 段玉裁 commentary
evidence.field: 作; Shuowen entry and commentary
evidence.text: The entry gives 作, 起也, ‘arise/begin,’ and says 从人从乍. Duan Yucai’s commentary cites classical glosses with related but distinguishable senses: 起 ‘rise,’ 為 ‘do,’ 始 ‘begin,’ and 生 ‘produce/be born.’ Duan reads 乍 as the phonetic element (从人，乍聲), while the received Shuowen head text does not state that explicitly. Its retrospective glosses should not be treated as proof of the graph’s earliest sense.
evidence.title: 說文解字「作」

evidence.source: 王子揚, “卜辭‘■不既作’試解,” 出土文獻 (第三輯), Tsinghua University-hosted PDF
evidence.field: 作; disputed oracle-bone graph readings and phonetic role
evidence.text: The article reviews a proposal by 曾憲通 that an oracle-bone graph was the original graph of 作 and represented a person using a hand-held implement to turn soil, but rejects that specific graph identification and interpretation as insufficiently supported. In its own discussion of another oracle-bone graph, the author argues that 乍 (read 作) functions as a phonetic in a compound; it cites oracle examples and contrasts the graph with other forms. The article interprets 作 in the discussed divination phrase as ‘arise/recover,’ while acknowledging uncertainty in graph identification. This is evidence for a disputed paleographic analysis, not a settled account of every early 作 form.
evidence.title: 卜辭“■不既作”試解

evidence.source: 普及版 字通, reproduced by Kotobank
evidence.field: 作; phonetic analysis and early uses
evidence.text: 字通 analyzes 作 as a phono-semantic graph with 乍 as sound component, and says 乍 was the earlier graph for 作. It reports oracle-bone uses of 乍 for constructing a structure or settlement, and bronze uses for casting a ritual vessel, building a settlement and broader making/action. This account supports distinguishing the early broad ‘make/work’ graph history from the later explicit 人+乍 analysis. The underlying ancient glyph images were not inspected here.

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction (2014), character table reproduced by University of Michigan
evidence.field: 乍; Middle Chinese and Old Chinese reconstruction
evidence.text: The table gives Mandarin zhà, Middle Chinese dzraeH, and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[dz]ˤrak-s for 乍, glossed ‘suddenly.’ The local baxter-sagart.tsv row supplied for 作 instead gives 作 zuò, MC tsak, OC *[ts]ˤak (and a departing-tone *[ts]ˤak-s reading). The systems’ forms are not identical: the displayed 乍 sudden-sense entry has a voiced affricate and -rak-s, while 作 has voiceless affricate and -ak. Do not silently claim exact phonological identity from these entries; a phonetic relationship can be graphically conventional or historically conditioned, but the retrieved evidence does not establish the sound change linking these particular reconstructions.

evidence.source: Contributor's source summary documented in the CUHK dictionary entry
evidence.field: 乍; graphic origin disagreement
evidence.text: The CUHK dictionary attributes to 吳其昌 an interpretation of the oracle-bone form as a knife cutting trees, and notes 裘錫圭’s view that the action includes cutting grass. The Academia Sinica character database instead calls 乍 an image of a garment collar and says it depicts making clothing. The CUHK page cites oracle examples and earlier scholarship for vegetation clearing; the garment account was inspected as text but its glyph images were not visually inspected. These competing object/graphic interpretations remain unresolved by this research.

evidence.source: Academia Sinica Character Database
evidence.field: 乍; proposed graphic origin and form sequence
evidence.text: This page labels 乍 as the original graph for 作 and interprets its oracle-bone form as an upper garment lapel, with a sense of making clothing; it says a person marker was later added to form 作. This conflicts with the CUHK account that reads the ancient form as cutting vegetation. The page presents Oracle, bronze, Chu manuscript and seal-script categories, but dates and specific glyph witnesses were not available in the opened text, and the glyph images were not visually inspected. The directional ancestor claim is therefore reported as that source’s proposal rather than adopted as established chronology.
